# #3726 -- the reported situation IS a statement about WHICH LAYER diagnoses this code, so
# one probe captures all three layers on the same source, for every compiler:
#
#   line 1  DXIL     the compile the issue says the *backend* rejects
#   line 2  SPIR-V   the compile the issue says succeeds instead of erroring
#   line 3  -fcgl    high-level IR only: the DXIL lowering passes never run, so a
#                    diagnostic here is a FRONT-END diagnostic and nothing else.
#                    This is the instrument that answers the title's question --
#                    "does Sema reject it?" -- rather than inferring it from message
#                    shape. Message shape does not work: the DXIL backend error is
#                    printed WITH a `repro.hlsl:15:10:` source location on main and
#                    WITHOUT one on v1.4.1907 ("Use /Zi for source location"), so a
#                    file:line prefix does not distinguish front end from back end.
#
# Line 1 alone is the report; see cmd-as-filed.txt. Lines 2 and 3 add layers, they do
# not alter line 1.
#
# The reporter names no profile. `float4 main(): SV_Target` plus `Sample` is a pixel
# shader, and ps_6_0 is the OLDEST profile that can express it, which keeps every
# release probeable instead of answering `invalid profile` (SKILL.md step 6).
#
# No -Vd, no -Zi, no other flags: the issue is about which layer speaks, so nothing
# that could silence a layer is added.
-T ps_6_0 -E main repro.hlsl
-T ps_6_0 -E main -spirv repro.hlsl
-T ps_6_0 -E main -fcgl repro.hlsl
